cards.headline: The mirror twin of 'Maps'
cards.snippet: 'Hysteric' is a love song with the desperation drained out of it. AllMusic's Heather Phares described it as 'a love song about being happy with someone rather than trying to make him or her stay' — the inverse of 'Maps,' the band's pleading signature ballad, where love is something begged for. Here the refrain is pure arrival: you suddenly complete me. Phares called 'Hysteric' the mirror twin of 'Maps' — the same devotion, answered instead of yearned for.
cards.context: AllMusic's review of It's Blitz! (Heather Phares), March 2009; full review text via the album's Qobuz page.

cards.headline: Packed for downtime, it became the album's sound
cards.snippet: It's Blitz! was largely written in the studio, and its defining sound arrived as luggage. Heading to Sonic Ranch in Tornillo, Texas, guitarist Nick Zinner packed a vintage ARP synthesizer that, as Classic Rock told it, 'was supposed to provide downtime entertainment, but ended up being the defining noise on It's Blitz!' Producer Nick Launay described songs assembling from chopped drum loops and jams: 'Karen [O] would listen to that and come up with a vocal melody and then suddenly everything would fall into place.' 'Hysteric' — co-produced by David Sitek, with saxophone and trumpet threaded through it — is that method at its most tender.
cards.context: Wikipedia's It's Blitz! article, drawing on Classic Rock's account of the 2008 Sonic Ranch sessions.

cards.headline: The refrain everyone quotes
cards.snippet: The song's refrain is its most-quoted line: two of the pool's top comments quote it word for word, and the higher-liked one (91 likes) names it a favorite lyric outright. The Village Voice heard the moment the same way in 2009, calling Karen O's repeated delivery 'this record's best mantra.'
cards.context: Two of the song's top comments quote the line word for word; @karlirae6423 (91 likes) names it a favorite lyric. The Village Voice called Karen O's delivery of it 'this record's best mantra' in 2009.

cards.headline: The dance-floor number, remade as a ballad
cards.snippet: The deluxe edition's acoustic remake of the album track: Karen O over acoustic guitar and strings, the synth ballad slowed and hushed. One of two acoustic versions the band released in 2009. One listener: "THERES AN ACOUSTIC VERSION?????"
cards.context: yeahyeahyeahsmusic, the band's official channel. 123,528 views, 21 comments observed Oct 30, 2026. A second acoustic take followed on iTunes Originals (4:10).

cards.headline: Sunny Dancer (2026) gives it a pre-party makeover
cards.snippet: About 32 minutes into George Jaques's Sunny Dancer, 'Hysteric' plays as Ivy (Bella Ramsey) and her roommate Ella (Ruby Stokes) do a makeover in their cabin before heading out to join the gang at camp.
cards.context: Documented by SeekerTune's timestamped soundtrack guide (the scene at 00:32:05); NME's soundtrack listing confirms the song.
